name: CTA-lockup
purpose: A call-to-action band: a heading, a supporting line, and a Button pair (secondary + primary), arranged for either a full-bleed marketing band (centred) or a narrower in-page band (title left, actions right). Composed ENTIRELY from the gated Button atom plus canon type composites — no new visual vocabulary, only arrangement. Wave-6 itinerary row 122 (Layer 2, class NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS at mint; PROPOSED here, not ruled).

props.name: arrangement
props.$note: Two arrangement variants drawn in the reference: A centred (full-bleed marketing band, everything centred), B split (title block left, action pair right, for a narrower in-page band). Structural variance, a VARIANTS-axis prop, same class as Page-header-lockup's own `arrangement` prop.

props.name: heading
props.$note: Plain, informational — no invented urgency copy (brief DO-NOT-RULE: mono discipline, no manufactured scarcity).

props.name: actions
props.$note: 1-2 Button instances. The organism does not draw a new button style; the specimen shows secondary+primary, but any tier combination is valid.

variants.name: centered
variants.use: A full-bleed marketing band — a page section whose whole job is the call to action.

variants.name: split
variants.use: A narrower in-page band — a call to action that sits between other content, e.g. at the end of an article or a feature grid.

tokens.heading: borrowed from canon/type.css .t-ed-heading-3 composite (24px/300, .em 400) — never a raw declaration
tokens.support: borrowed from canon/type.css .t-ed-body composite (16px/400) — never a raw declaration
tokens.band: surface/subtle — the same token Footer's own band uses, so a CTA band and a footer band read as the same family of neutral section
tokens.$note: Every token above resolves through the ATOM's own manifest or the type-composite ramp; this organism binds nothing new beyond `--band`, itself an alias of an existing token. The lock-up's own CSS (`.ctal-*`) is flex arrangement only.

responsive.$status: PROPOSED at #210 wave-6 (not ruled) — reflow verified in a real browser at 3 widths.
responsive.rule: Wide: split form shows title left / actions right, one row; centred form is already centred at every width. Container <=560px (container-query, WCAG 1.4.10 reachable to 320px): the split form collapses to the centred stacked form, and the button pair goes full-width stacked in BOTH arrangements — the same 560px threshold Page-header-lockup uses for its own action row.
responsive.$note: s210-D3 discipline: the lock-up declares no width of its own; the container gives it one.

commonPatterns: marketing band with a single action pair

accessibility.structure: The heading is a single semantic heading level per instance; the organism does not assert which level (h1/h2) — that depends on the page it sits in.
accessibility.focus: Both buttons keep Button's OWN :focus-visible ring — the organism adds no new focusable element and no new focus style.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: No RAG value appears anywhere in this component — mono discipline (brief DO-NOT-RULE).

antiPatterns: Re-drawing the button CSS instead of composing the existing Button atom
Giving the lock-up a fixed width — s210-D3 reserves that for the container
Inventing urgency copy — a countdown, an exclamation mark, manufactured scarcity — the brief's DO-NOT-RULE names this explicitly
Adding a third button — the organism draws exactly one action pair; a row needing more belongs to a different pattern
